questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The straight wire $A B$ carries a current $I$. The ends of the wire subtend angles $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ at the point $P$ as shown in figure. The magnetic field at the point $P$ is
questions.solution: The magnetic field at a point $P$ due to a current carrying straight wire, such that the ends of the wires, makes angle $\alpha$ and $\beta$ (see figure) is given by $B=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4 \pi d}(\sin \alpha-\sin \beta)$ where, $d$ is the distance between the point $P$ and wire. In the given problem, $\alpha=\theta_1$ and \beta=\theta_2\therefore \quad B=$\frac{\mu_0 I}{4 \pi d} \left(\sin \theta_1-\sin$ \theta_2\right)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A long straight wire of radius a carries a steady current 1. The current is uniformly distributed across its cross section. The ratio of the magnetic field at $\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2}$ and 2a from axis of the wire is:
questions.solution:
Magnetic field due to straight wire,
$B=\frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r}$
Magnetic field at $\frac{a}{2}$ is,
$\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{a} / 2}=\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{I}}{2 \pi(\mathrm{a} / 2)}\therefore \frac{\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{a} / 2}}{\mathrm{ B}_{2 \mathrm{a}}}=\frac{1}{1}=1: 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The electrostatic force $\left(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}_1\right)$ and magnetic force $\left(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}_2\right)$ acting on a charge q moving with velocity v can be written:
questions.solution:
Electrostatic force, $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}_1=\mathrm{q} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}$
Magnetic force, $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}_2=\mathrm{q}(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{V}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}})$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic moments associated with two closely wound circular coils A and B of radius $r_A=10 \mathrm{ cm}$ and $r_B=20 \mathrm{ cm}$ respectively are equal if: (Where $\mathrm{N}_A, \mathrm{I}_A$ and $\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{B}}, \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{B}}$ are number of turn and current of $A$ and $B$ respectively)
questions.solution:
The magnetic moment associated with circular coil,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & M=N I A \\ \\ & M_A=M_B \\ \\ & \therefore N_A I_A A_A=N_B I_B A_B \\ \\ & \therefore N_A I_A \pi(0.1)^2=N_B I_B \pi(0.2)^2\left(\because A=\pi r^2\right) \\ \\ & \therefore N_A I_A=4 N_B I_B \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solenoid of 1200 turns is wound uniformly in a single layer on a glass tube $2 \mathrm{ m}$ long and $0.2 \mathrm{ m}$ in diameter. The magnetic intensity at the center of the solenoid when a current of 2 A flows through it is:
questions.solution:
Given that number of turns, $n=1200$
Current, $\mathrm{I}=2 \mathrm{ A}$
Magnetic field at centre inside the solenoid is given by,
$\mathrm{B}=\mu_0 \mathrm{nI}$
So magnetic intensity at centre of the solenoid,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathrm{H}=\frac{\mathrm{B}}{\mu_0}=\mathrm{nI}=\left(\frac{1200}{2}\right)(2) \quad\left(\because \mathrm{B}=\mu_0 \mathrm{H}\right) \\ \\ & \mathrm{H}=1.2 \times 10^3 \mathrm{Am}^{-1} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charge particle is moving in a uniform magnetic field $(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}) \mathrm{T}$. If it has an acceleration of $(\alpha \hat{i}-4 \hat{j}) \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^2$, then the value of $\alpha$ will be :
questions.solution:
Given that uniform magnetic field, $\vec{B}=(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}) T$
Acceleration $\vec{a}=(\alpha \hat{i}-4 \hat{j}) \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ We know that
$F=q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) \Rightarrow m \vec{a}=q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$
Here, $\vec{a} \perp \vec{B}$, so, $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{B}=0$
$(\alpha \hat{i}-4 \hat{j})(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j})=0 \Rightarrow 2 \alpha-12=0 \Rightarrow \alpha=6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic moment of an electron (e) revolving in an orbit around nucleus with an orbital angular momentum is given by:
questions.solution:
As $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}=\mathrm{IA}$
$\Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}|=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{v}}} \pi \mathrm{R}^2\left[\because \mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{\mathrm{T}}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{V}}}\right]$
$\Rightarrow|\vec{M}|=\frac{1}{2} e v R \Rightarrow|\vec{M}|=\frac{\mathrm{mvR}}{1} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{e}}{2 \mathrm{ m}}$
$\Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}|=\frac{\mathrm{eL}}{2 \mathrm{ m}} \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}|=-\frac{\mathrm{e} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{L}}}{2 \mathrm{ m}}$
[\because$ Here \overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{L}}$ will always be opposite]

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A proton moving with a velocity $3 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ enters a magnetic field of $0.3$ tesla at an angle of $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the field. The radius of curvature of its path will be $(\mathrm{e} / \mathrm{m}$ for proton $=10^{8} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{kg}$ )
questions.solution: $r=\frac{m v \sin \theta}{\mathrm{B} e}=\frac{3 \times 10^{5} \sin 30^{{}^{\circ}}}{0.3 \times 10^{8}}\frac{3 \times 10^{5} \times \frac{1}{2}}{3 \times 10^{7}}=0.5 \times 10^{-2}m=0.5 \mathrm{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solenoid is $2 \mathrm{ m}$ long and $3 \mathrm{ cm}$ in diameter. It has 5 layers of winding of 1000 turns each and carries a current of $5 \mathrm{ A}$. What is the magnetic field at its centre ? Use the standard value of $\mu_{0}$.
questions.solution: Length of solenoid, $l=2 \mathrm{ m}$ Total number of turns, $\mathrm{N}=5 \times 1000=5000$ Number of turns per unit length, $\mathrm{n}=\frac{\mathrm{N}}{l}=\frac{5000}{2}=2500 \mathrm{ m}^{-1}$ Current, I = 5A Now, B $=\mu_{0} \mathrm{nI}=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 2500 \times 5 \mathrm{ T}=1.57 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{ T}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron revolves in a circular orbit of radius $r$ with angular speed $\omega$. The magnetic field at the centre of electron orbit is
questions.solution:
Magnetic field at the centre of circular loop.

$B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}l}{2r}... \left(i\right)$

Period of revolution of electron, where $\omega =$ angular velocity of electron

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{ω}$

where, $\omega =$ angular velocity of electron.

Current produced due to movement of electron,

$I = \dfrac{e}{T} = \dfrac{e}{2\pi\omega} = \dfrac{e\omega}{2\pi}$

On substituting the value of $I$ in Eq. (i), we get

$B = \dfrac{\mu0}{2r} \cdot \dfrac{e\omega}{2\pi}$

$⇒ B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}e\omega}{4\pir}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two electrons are moving with equal speed of $5 \times {10}^{5}ms^{- 1}$ parallel to each other. The ratio of the electrostatic to& the magnetic force between them is
questions.solution:
Given, speed of electrons, $v = 5 \times {10}^{5}ms^{- 1}$

Electrostatic force between the electrons,

${F}_{e} = k \cdot \dfrac{e2}{r2}... \left(i\right)$

Magnetic field produced due to moving electron with velocity $v$,

$B = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi} \cdot \dfrac{ev}{r2}...\left(ii\right)$

Magnetic force between the electrons,

${F}_{m} = Bev = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi} \cdot \dfrac{ev}{r2} \cdot ev$ & (from Eq. (ii))

${F}_{m} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi} \cdot \dfrac{e^{2}v^{2}}{r2}$

$∴$ From Eqs. (i) and (iii), we have

$\dfrac{Fe}{Fm} = \dfrac{ke^{2} / r^{2}}{{μ}_{0}e^{2}v^{2}4\pi \cdot r^{2}} = \dfrac{k \cdot 4\pi}{{μ}_{0}v^{2}}$

$= \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{9} \times 4 \times 3. 14}{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}\left(5 \times {10}^{5}\right)^{2}} = 3. 6 \times {10}^{5}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre $O$& of& the current-carrying square loop shown in the figure& is
questions.solution:
Given, current through the square loop is $2A$.

$I = 2A$

The given situation is shown in the figure. Magnetic field due to wire $AB$ at the centre $O$ is

${B}_{AB} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi} \cdot \dfrac{I}{r} \left[sin45 ° + sin45 °\right]$

$= {10}^{- 7} \times \dfrac{2}{2 \times {10}^{- 2}}\left[\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$

$= \sqrt{2} \times {10}^{- 5}T$ [Downward to the plane of square loop]

Since, magnetic field due to side $AB, BC, CD$ and $DA$ is same in magnitude and direction.

Hence, net magnetic field at $O$

$B = 4 \times {B}_{AB} = 4\sqrt{2} \times {10}^{- 5}T$

questions.q: A proton is revolving on a circular path of radius $2$ mm with frequency $10$ Hz. Magnetic dipole moment associated with proton is
questions.solution:
Given, charge on proton, $q = e$
$= 1. 6 \times {10}^{- 19}C$

Radius, $r = 2mm = 2 \times {10}^{- 3}cm$

Frequency, $f = 10Hz$

Current associated by proton is given by

$= 1. 6 $\times {10}^{- 19} \times10 = 1. 6 \times {10}^{- 18}$ A$

$= 2 \times {10}^{- 24}A - m^{2}$

questions.q: A current $i$ flows through a loop as shown in figure. The magnetic field at the Centre $O$ is
questions.solution:

$= \dfrac{{μ}_{o}i}{8r} $\$left[\dfrac{1}{3} +$3\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio of angular momentum $L$ to the atomic dipole moment ${μ}_{i}$ for hydrogen like atoms and ions is
options: always constant and is equal to the ratio of mass to the charge of electron
always constant and is equal to twice the ratio of mass to the charge of electron to the principal quantum number $n$
proportional to the principal quantum number $n$
questions.solution:
The electron moving with a speed $v$ in the circular Bohr orbit of radius $r$ constitutes a current of magnitude.

$i = \dfrac{e}{T}.$ where $T$ is the orbital period of the electron.

$T = 2\pir / v$

$i = \dfrac{ev}{2\pir}$

By definition of atomic dipole moment ${μ}_{i},$ its magnitude is given by

${μ}_{i} = iA = \dfrac{eV}{2\pir} \cdot \pir^{2} = \dfrac{evr}{2}$

$∴$ Angular momentum, $L = mvr$
$∴ \dfrac{L}{\mui} = \dfrac{2mvr}{evr} = \dfrac{2m}{e} = \text{constant}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A copper rod of mass $m$ slides under gravity on two smooth parallel rails $l$ distance apart and set an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. At the bottom, the rails are joined by a resistance $R$ in figure. There is a uniform magnetic field $B$ perpendicular& to the plane of the rails. The terminal velocity of rod is
questions.solution:
Terminal velocity of the rod is attained when magnetic force on the rod (Bil)& balances the component of weight of the rod$( mgsin\theta ) ,$ as in figure.

So, $Bil = mgsin\theta$

$B\left(\dfrac{e}{R}\right)l = mgsin\theta$

$\dfrac{Ble}{R} = mgsin\theta$

$\dfrac{Bl\left(B / {V}_{T}\right)}{R} = mgsin\theta$

${v}_{T} = \dfrac{mgsin\thetaR}{B^{2}l^{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: To increase the current sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer by $50 % ,$& its resistance is increased, so that new resistance becomes twice its initial resistance, by what factor does its voltage sensitivity change?
questions.solution:
New, current sensitivity, ${I}_s^{'} = {I}_{s} + \dfrac{50}{100}{I}_{s}$

$= \dfrac{150}{100}{I}_{s} = \dfrac{3}{2}{I}_{s}$

New resistance, $R^{'} = 2R$

Initial voltage sensitivity, ${V}_{s} = \dfrac{Is}{R}$

Now, new voltage sensitivity.

${V}_{s} = {i}_s^{'}R^{'} = \dfrac{\dfrac{3}{2}{I}_{c}}{2R} = \dfrac{3}{4}{V}_{s}$

$%$ decrease in voltage sensitivity

$= \dfrac{{V}_{s} - {V}_s^{'}}{Vs} \times 100$

$= \left(1 - \dfrac{Vs}{Vs}\right) \times 100$

$= \left(1 - \dfrac{3}{4}\right) \times 100 = 25 %$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A positive charge $q$ is projected in magnetic field of width $\dfrac{mv}{\sqrt{2}qB}$ with velocity $v$. Then, the time taken by charged particle to emerge from the magnetic field is
questions.solution:
Referring the diagram,&

width of magnetic field $w = \dfrac{mv}{\sqrt{2}qB}$

Also we know that when a charge is projected in perpendicular magnetic field then radius of path is

$R = \dfrac{mv}{qB}$

Now in triangle OAB,

$sin\theta = \dfrac{w}{R} = \dfrac{mv\sqrt{2}qB}{mvqB}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ sin\theta = sin45 °$

$= sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Time period for angle $2\pi$ is $T = \dfrac{2\pim}{qB}$

$∴$ Time by charged particle for $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ in order to emerge from magnetic field is&

$T = \dfrac{\pim}{4qB}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A coil in the shape of an equilateral triangle of side $l$ is suspended between the pole pieces of a permanent magnet such that $B$ is in plane of the coil. If due to a current $i$ in the triangle, a torque $τ$ rests on it, the side $l$ of the triangle is
questions.solution:
Torque acting on equilateral triangle in a magnetic field $B$ is

$τ = iABsin\theta$

Area of triangle $LMN$,

$A = \dfrac{3}{2}l^{2}$ and $\theta = 90 °$

Substituting the given values in expression for torque, we get

$τ = i \times \dfrac{3}{4}l^{2}Bsin90 °$

$τ = \dfrac{3}{4}il^{2}B$~ $\left(∵ sin90 ° = 1\right)$

$l^{2} = \dfrac{4τ}{\sqrt{3}Bi}$

Here, $l = 2\left(\dfrac{τ}{\sqrt{3}Bi}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charged particle moving in a uniform magnetic field and losses $4 \%$ of its kinetic energy. The radius of curvature of its path changes by
questions.solution: As we know $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{qvB}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}^{2}}{\mathrm{r}}\therefore \mathrm{r}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{Bq}}$ And $\mathrm{KE}=\mathrm{k}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^{2}\therefore \mathrm{mv}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{ km}}\therefore \mathrm{r}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}}=\frac{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{ km}}}{\mathrm{qB}}\Rightarrow r \propto \sqrt{k}$ or $r=c^{1 / 2}(c$ is a constant $)\frac{\mathrm{dr}}{\mathrm{dr}}=\mathrm{c} \frac{\mathrm{dk}^{1 / 2}}{\mathrm{dr}}$ or $\frac{\mathrm{c} \Delta \mathrm{k}}{\Delta \mathrm{r}}=2 \sqrt{\mathrm{k}}\frac{\Delta r}{r}=\frac{\mathrm{c} \Delta \mathrm{k}}{2 \sqrt{\mathrm{k}} \mathrm{c} \sqrt{\mathrm{k}}}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{k}}{2 \mathrm{k}}$ Therefore percentage changes in radius of path, $\frac{\Delta r}{r} \times 100=\frac{\Delta k}{2 k} \times 100=2 \%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two particles $\mathrm{X}$ and $\mathrm{Y}$ having equal charges, after being accelerated through the same potential difference, enter a region of uniform magnetic field and describe circular paths of radii $\mathrm{R}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{R}_{2}$, respectively. The ratio of masses of $\mathrm{X}$ and $\mathrm{Y}$ is
questions.solution:
When a charge particle is allowed to move in a uniform magnetic field, then it describes spiral or circular path

$$

\begin{array}{l}

\text{ Centripetal force, } \frac{\mathrm{mv}^{2}}{\mathrm{R}}=\mathrm{qvB} \quad \therefore \\

\mathrm{v}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{qB}}{\mathrm{m}} \mathrm{R}\right) \\

\text{ Hence, } \sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{q} \mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{m}}}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{qB}}{\mathrm{m}}\right) \mathrm{R}\left[\because \mathrm{V}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{qV}}{\mathrm{m}}}\right] \\

\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}=\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{mV}}{\mathrm{q}}\right)^{1 / 2} \times \frac{1}{\mathrm{~B}} \\

\text{ or, } \mathrm{m} \propto \mathrm{R}^{2}

\end{array}

$$

$[\because \mathrm{V}, \mathrm{q}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ are constant $]$

$$

\text{ or, } \frac{\mathrm{m}_{1}}{\mathrm{~m}_{2}}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}_{1}}{\mathrm{R}_{2}}\right)^{2}

$$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A long straight wire along the $Z$ -axis carries a current I in the negative $Z$ -direction. The magnetic vector field $\vec{B}$ at a point having coordinates $(x, y)$ in the $Z=0$ plane is
questions.solution:
The wire carries a current $I$ in the negative $z$ -direction. We have to consider the magnetic vector field $\vec{B}$ at $(x, y)$ in the $z=0$ plane.
Magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is perpendicular to $O P\therefore \vec{B}=B \sin \theta \hat{i}-B \cos \theta \hat{j} \begin{array}{l} \sin \theta=\frac{y}{r}, \cos \theta=\frac{x}{r}B=\frac{\mu_{0} I}{2 \pi r}\\ \therefore \quad \vec{B}=\frac{\mu_{0} I}{2 \pi r^{2}}( y \hat{i}-x \hat{j}) \end{array} or $\quad $\vec{B}=\frac{\mu_{0} I(y \hat{i}-x \hat{j})}{2 \pi \left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A narrow beam of protons and deuterons, each having the same momentum, enters a region of uniform magnetic field directed perpendicular to their direction of momentum. The ratio of the radii of the circular paths described by them is
questions.solution: Since, the radius of circular path of a charged particle in magnetic field is $\mathrm{r}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}}=\frac{\rho}{\mathrm{qB}}$ Now, the radius of circular path of charged particle of given momentum $\rho$ and magnetic field $\mathrm{B}$ is given by $\mathrm{r} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{q}}$ But charge on both charged particles, protons and deuterons, is same. Therefore, $\frac{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{D}}}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{D}}}{\mathrm{q}_{\rho}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{l}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two parallel conductors carry current in opposite directions as shown in figure. One conductor carries a current of $10.0 \mathrm{ A}$. Point $\mathrm{C}$ is a distance $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{2}$ to the right of the $10.0 \mathrm{ A}$ current. If $\mathrm{d}=18 \mathrm{ cm}$ and I is adjusted so that the magnetic field at $\mathrm{Cis}$ zero, the value of the current $I$ is
questions.solution: The magnetic field at $\mathrm{C}$ due to first conductor is $\mathrm{B}_{1}=\frac{\mu_{0}}{2 \pi} \frac{\mathrm{I}}{3 \mathrm{ d} / 2}$ (since, point $\mathrm{C}$ is separated by $\mathrm{d}+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{2}=\frac{3 \mathrm{ d}}{2}$ from 1 st conductor). The direction of field is perpendicular to the plane of paper and directed outwards. The magnetic field at $\mathrm{C}$ due to second conductor is $\mathrm{B}_{2}=\frac{\mu_{0}}{2 \pi} \frac{10}{\mathrm{ d} / 2}$ (since, point $\mathrm{C}$ is separated by $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{2}$ from 2 nd conductor) The direction of field is perpendicular to the plane of paper and directed inwards. Since, direction of $\mathrm{B}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{B}_{2}$ at point $\mathrm{C}$ is in opposite direction and the magnetic field at C is zero, therefore, $\begin{array}{c}\mathrm{B}_{1}=\mathrm{B}_{2}$\\ $\frac{\mu_{0}}{2 \pi} \frac{\mathrm{I}}{3 \mathrm{ d} / 2}=\frac{\mu_{0}}{2 \pi} \frac{10}{\mathrm{ d} / 2} \end{array}$ On solving $\mathrm{I}=30.0 \mathrm{ A}$

questions.q: A conducting circular loop of radius $r$ carries a constant current $i.$ It is placed in a uniform magnetic field $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}_{0}$ such that $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}_{0}$ is perpendicular to the plane of the loop. The magnetic force acting on the loop is
questions.solution: The magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the paper. Let us consider two diametrically opposite elements. By Fleming's Left hand rule on element $\mathrm{AB}$ the direction of force will be Leftwards and the magnitude will be $\mathrm{dF}=\operatorname{Idl} \mathrm{B} \sin90^{{}^{\circ}}=\mathrm{IdIB}$
